newsitem.title: USA: U.S. policy on dollar unchanged, Rubin says.
newsitem.headline: U.S. policy on dollar unchanged, Rubin says.

text.p: The U.S. policy on the dollar remains unchanged, Treasury Secretary Robert Rubin said on Wednesday.
"Our dollar policy is unchanged," he told public television's Nightly Business Report program.
In the past, Rubin has touted the benefits of a strong dollar, saying it was in the U.S. interest because it keeps inflation and interest rates down.
Rubin was upbeat about the outlook for the U.S. economy, saying he sees solid growth and low inflation.
"They (the U.S. economic prospects) look quite good," he said. "American business certainly seems to be competitive across a broad array of industries.
"I think we're well positioned going forward," he added.

Rubin declined to respond directly when asked whether Japan could stop the dollar's relentless rise against the yen without the help of the United States, saying he does not comment on the "dynamics" of markets.
